title: The labels a reading gave up on can be found
goal: Read every label in a separated screenshot and a line tells you how it went: so many came back as text, three stayed pictures. Those three are the ones you have to deal with by hand, and the app will not tell you which they are. The only way to find them is to scroll the layers list looking for rows still called Text and guess. Make the count the way to them: press it and those are what you have picked.
notes: From the rough list of queue/audits/2026-09-17-read-every-label.json: "A label that stayed a picture is counted and not pointed at. The line says 3 stayed pictures and there is no way to jump to them, so finding them means looking at the layers list for rows that are still called Text." Its next rough line explains why nothing is selected after the batch, and that reasoning still holds: moving the selection onto one of forty labels nobody asked about would be the app pointing at the wrong thing. This is the opposite case, where the person has asked. The pill is the shared canvas notice (Sources/Photonz/EditorView.swift canvasNoticeChip, subject .turnedIntoTextInBatch in Sources/PhotonzCore/CopyConfirmation.swift) and it already knows how to carry a pressable action, so this is an action on the existing notice rather than new chrome. It depends on a-notice-at-the-foot-of-the-canvas-stops-swallow being done first, because that one changes which part of the pill takes the pointer.
acceptance: The part of the line that counts what stayed a picture can be pressed, and pressing it picks exactly those layers and brings them into view
It looks pressable before you press it and reads as one sentence, not as a control bolted onto a report
Nothing is picked or scrolled when the reading did what it was asked and nothing stayed a picture: the line stays a plain report

Try it: Next release, turn on Read every label in a separated screenshot at once (next-read-every-label), separate a dense screenshot, read every label, and press the count of what stayed a picture. Those layers are picked
A walk covers it, and it is named on the task with queue.mjs walks
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Adversarial review BEFORE building: the task asked for the count in the line to be pressable, which fights the rule the dependency task had just enforced (only a BUTTON in the pill takes the pointer, everything else is click-through). Considered a capsule button on the end saying Select Them instead: rejected, because a report that counts three strays and then offers a separate control is two things to read where there is one thing to do, and it would have put another dead patch on the pill. Took the narrower version: the words that count are the way to them, in the accent colour under a line, and every other word in the pill stays click-through. Shortest version that delivers the value, and a-notice-lets-a-click-through-walk still passes unchanged.

Scoped out on purpose: a reading where NOTHING came back. Its line is 'None of the 12 labels could be read', one sentence about the whole ask with no count to pick out and nothing to pick them out from, so TextReading.Batch.stillPicturesTail is nil there and the pill offers nothing. Covered by the unit test aReadingThatLandedNothingHasNoTail. Noted in the audit's rough list.

Tried and reverted: a steady playtest name (@stayed-pictures) on the link, so a walk would not have to spell the count. press refuses a steady name on a CONTROL by design (PlaytestHarness.pressTarget: a steady name names the row a control sits on), and letting it through would have meant new harness plumbing for one walk. The walk names the words instead, and the expectNotice step right above it already pins the exact sentence, so it is no more fragile than the assertion beside it.

Proved two step kinds safe under a screen lock and added them to PlaytestLockSafety.stepsThatSurviveALock: expectNotice and expectInView. Both read the app rather than accessibility (the pill's own sentence; a control's geometry out of the register press already uses). Watched working in find-what-stayed-a-picture-walk, 30 steps, forced with PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1 on a Mac locked since 2026-09-14; the walk then ran unforced and reported lockSafe true, status ok.

left rough: pressing the count takes the pill away and nothing remembers which labels a reading gave up on, so there is no way back to the count once it has faded. It is in the audit's rough list for the user to react to; it did not earn its own task because the same six-second clock is how every notice in the app works and changing it is a question about notices, not about this line.

left rough: the layers list can only show one of the three at a time on this capture (they are six rows apart, the list holds five). The canvas covers for it by outlining all three. Changing revealInLayersList's policy would reach every caller of it, which is out of scope here; in the audit's rough list.
